subject: English
central_question: How do adolescent fantasy, hero worship and limited social opportunity shape Sophie’s dreams, relationships and eventual disappointment?
in_scope_units: About A.R. Barton and the themes of adolescent fantasising and hero worship.
Sophie and Jansie’s different attitudes to future work and the biscuit factory.
Sophie’s working-class home, her parents and her attraction to Geoff’s silent unknown world.
The claimed meeting with Danny Casey and the family’s disbelief.
The football match, the spread of the story and Sophie’s secret expectations.
The canal-side wait, Danny’s failure to appear and Sophie’s return to fantasy.
Character, socio-economic background, metaphorical expressions, present participles, colloquial speech and writing tasks.
banned_topics: A factual biography of Mary Quant, Tom Finney or Danny Casey beyond references in the story.
A general history of football or the World Cup beyond Sophie’s family conversations.

known_pitfalls.claim: Sophie and Jansie share the same attitude to the future.
known_pitfalls.correction: Sophie fantasises about glamorous careers; Jansie accepts their likely work at the biscuit factory.
He wants to believe but repeatedly calls it unlikely and doubts that Casey will come.

known_pitfalls.claim: Sophie certainly meets Danny Casey in the arcade.
known_pitfalls.correction: The story’s ending and her known fantasising indicate that the meeting is imagined; the match is her only real sight of him.

known_pitfalls.claim: The story mocks every adolescent dream.
known_pitfalls.correction: It distinguishes creative aspiration from fantasy that ignores reality and produces self-deception.

known_pitfalls.claim: Sophie’s family is wealthy enough to support a boutique.
known_pitfalls.correction: The cramped home, factory prospects and father’s response show financial limitation.

recommended_example_progression: Use the first Think as you read questions to compare Sophie and Jansie.
Use Understanding the text Q4 to establish the family’s economic background.
Use the middle comprehension questions to examine Geoff’s belief and Sophie’s secrecy.
Use the final Think as you read questions to decide whether the meeting occurred.
Use Working with words and Noticing form for metaphor, slang and present participles.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with Understanding the text Questions 1–4, Talking about the text, Working with words, Noticing form, Thinking about language, Writing and Things to do.
